mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A severe hail/wind threat will expand east-southeastward across northern Indiana into western Ohio this evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: A severe hail/wind threat will expand east-southeastward across northern Indiana into western Ohio this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms have increased in coverage this evening across northern IN, likely aided by a weak mid-level disturbance noted on water vapor satellite imagery upstream across IL. Initial cells have undergone mergers, with multiple clusters ongoing. Ample low-level moisture and related very strong buoyancy will continue to support vigorous updrafts, even though stronger mid-level flow and related deep-layer shear will tend to remain a bit displaced to the north of the surface warm sector. Even so, enough shear should be present to support a mix of supercells and multicells in the short term (reference recent VWPs from KIWX). Severe hail generally up to 1-1.5 inches in diameter will be possible with any cells that can remain at least semi-discrete, while damaging winds may occur with any small clusters moving east-southeastward. An increase in the severe wind potential may develop across parts of northeast IN into northwest OH if a more dominant cluster can become established, as some short-term guidance suggests

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for severe wind gusts is gradually waning across portions of the central High Plains. However, some potential will persist for the next 1-2 hours before the onset of nocturnal cooling

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has begun to wane across northeast CO and much of the NE Panhandle with the exception of a cluster of storms over Cherry county, NE. This trend is largely due to the prevalence of expanding cold pools across the region with some locations observing temperature falls on the order of 10-15 F within the cold pools. Although some re-development is possible along the edges of the cold pools and/or along colliding outflow boundaries, the spatial extent of the deeply-mixed warm sector is quickly becoming limited. Some severe downburst potential should persist for the next 1-2 hours where outflow propagation and/or convective overturning has not yet occurred, but the onset of nocturnal cooling beyond 02 UTC will act to increase inhibition and further reduce the potential for deep convection. Northeastern portions of WW 559 will likely see a more prolonged severe wind, and perhaps hail, threat heading into the late evening hours where deep convection continues to mature on the western periphery of a more moist and strongly sheared air mass
